evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The manager_restarted predicate (lines 1104-1116) only requires positive, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. It never compares boot IDs, even though the reboot snapshots carry boot_id and their check (lines 1117-1124) explicitly verifies boot identity. If the guest reboots between the manager 'before' and 'after' inspections, the new boot supplies a different manager PID and invocation ID, so the check reports an isolated manager restart that the evidence does not support; the later planned reboot can still satisfy its own boot_id_changed check. This is an implementation gap in the existing check's intent (proving a command-initiated manager restart), not a new requirement. The smallest fix is to require nonempty, equal boot IDs in the manager snapshot pair while retaining the PID and invocation-ID conditions.
